data.text:
Anil Kumar Rawat vs State Of Up And 4 Others on 9 May, 2024 
Author: Dinesh Pathak
Bench: Dinesh Pathak
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:83674
Court No. - 6
Case :- Writ - C No. - 12963 of 2024
Petitioner :- Anil Kumar Rawat
Respondent :- State Of Up And 4 Others
Counsel for Petitioner :- Sanjeev Kumar Khare 
Counsel for Respondent :- C.S.C.
Hon'ble Dinesh Pathak,J.
1.  Supplementary affidavit filed on behalf of the petitioner and copy of instructions dated 10.04.2024 duly signed by designated officer, Food Safety and Drugs Administration, filed by learned Standing Counsel are taken on record. 
2. Petitioner has invoked the extra-ordinary jurisdiction of this Court under Article 226 of the Constitution of India assailing the order dated 19.03.2024, whereby learned Commissioner (respondent no.2) has reviewed the earlier order dated 31.01.2024.
3. In view of the peculiar facts and circumstances of the present case and order proposed to be passed hereinunder, this Court proceeds to decide the instant writ petition finally without calling for respective affidavits between the parties, with the consent of the counsels present. 
Anil Kumar Rawat vs State Of Up And 4 Others on 9 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65484542/
1 4. It evince from the record that food license granted to the petitioner under the Food Safety &
Standard Act, 2006 (in brevity 'Act, 2006') has been suspended vide order dated 19.12.2022 (Annexure No.4). Having been aggrieved with the said order, petitioner has preferred an appeal. 
Appellate Court, vide order dated 31.01.2024 (Annexsure No.8), has allowed the appeal and quashed the suspension order dated 19.12.2022. It appears that, at later stage, designated officer under the Act, 2006 has filed a review application dated 06.02.2024. Learned Commissioner, vide order dated 19.03.2024, has allowed the review application and quashed the order dated 31.01.2024, which is under question before this Court. 
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner has advanced two fold submissions; first, no opportunity has been accorded to the petitioner before passing the order dated 19.03.2024 and second, there is no provision in the Act, 2006 for review of the order passed by the authority concerned.
6. Per contra, learned Standing Counsel has vehemently opposed the submission as advanced by learned counsel for the petitioner and supported the order impugned dated 19.03.2024. 
7. Having considered the rival submissions advanced by learned counsel for the parties and perusal of record, it is evident that order impugned dated 19.03.2024 has been passed ex-parte behind the back of the petitioner sans opportunity of hearing accorded to him. In penultimate paragraph of the order dated 19.03.2024, learned Commissioner has unequivocally observed that designated officer is present, however, neither Mr. Anil Kumar Rawat nor his counsel is present. Order dated 19.03.2024 further reveals that designated officer has filed the application (review) on 06.02.2024. 
On the date fixed for hearing i.e. 18.03.2024 designated officer was present, however, none was present on behalf of the petitioner. There is no observation qua issuance of notice to the petitioner and it's service upon him for hearing on review application dated 06.02.2024. There is nothing on the record to demonstrate that petitioner has deliberately ignored the proceeding before learned Commissioner despite full knowledge about the filing of the review application and date of hearing i.e. 18.03.2024, thus, it is evident that order dated 19.03.2024 is passed ex-parte against the petitioner sans opportunity of hearing accorded to him. While confronted with learned Standing Counsel on the point of opportunity of hearing, as submitted by learned counsel for the petitioner,
he could not rebut such fact. So far as the maintainability of the review application is concerned, it is open for the petitioner to raise this objection before the appellate court. 
8. In this conspectus, as above, in my considered opinion, present writ petition deserves to be allowed on the limited point of opportunity of hearing. 
9. As such, instant writ petition succeeds and is allowed. Order impugned dated 19.03.2024 passed by learned Commissioner Food Safety & Drugs Administration U.P. Lucknow (respondent no.2) is quashed. Proceeding initiated on the basis of the review application dated 06.02.2024 moved by designated officer is restored to its original number and parties are relegate before learned Commissioner, who shall reconsider the said review application dated 06.02.2024 and pass afresh order. 
Anil Kumar Rawat vs State Of Up And 4 Others on 9 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65484542/
2 10. Petitioner is hereby directed to present/appear on 29.05.2024 before Commissioner, Food Safety & Drugs Administration, Sector-C, Aliganj, Lucknow (respondent no.2), who has passed the order impugned, and file his detailed reply/objection to the review application dated 06.02.2024 moved by designated officer. After receiving the said reply/objection, learned Commissioner shall fix a date for final hearing and make endeavour to decide the aforesaid proceeding, in accordance with law, expeditiously, preferably within a period of two months. 
11. It is expected that it should be decided by a reasoned and speaking order, in accordance with law,
after affording opportunity of hearing to the parties concerned without granting unnecessary adjournments to either of the parties. 
12. With the aforesaid direction, present writ petition is disposed of. 
Order Date :- 9.5.2024 Jitendra  Anil Kumar Rawat vs State Of Up And 4 Others on 9 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65484542/
